newsitem.title: CHINA: Shanghai copper ends mixed on uncertainty.
newsitem.headline: Shanghai copper ends mixed on uncertainty.

text.p: Shanghai copper futures ended mixed in slow trading on Monday on uncertainty over the short-term market trend, traders said.
The most active February 1997 contract ended at 19,360 yuan ($2,333) per tonne, down 10 yuan. It opened down at 19,190 yuan, hitting an intra-day low of 19,160 and a high of 19,380.
November rose 20 to 18,970, December fell 60 to 19,100, January 50 to 19,350, March up 20 to 19,380, April down 20 to 19,360 and May 10 to 19,390.
Combined volume fell sharply to 20,450 tonnes from 87,200.

Copper opened lower due to last Friday's losses on the London Metal Exchange and moved in a narrow range of 100 yuan for the whole session, with many investors staying on the sidelines due to a lack of market-moving news.
"Retail investors dominated today's trade, with the short-term market trend unclear," one trader said.
"Over-supply of spot copper was the major factor limiting the potential of Shanghai copper to rise," he added.
Price of spot copper is around 19,300 yuan per tonne in Shanghai.
Traders said LME was still the most important factor influencing Shanghai copper in the short term in the absence of domestic market-moving news.
Aluminium ended mixed. November fell 30 to 13,450 yuan per tonne, December rose 80 to 13,400 and January 50 to 13,400.
Combined volume rose to 1,080 tonnes from 700.
